headline: Embodied First Exam brings coding-agent evaluation to diverse simulated robots
summary: A Nov. 9 arXiv preprint introduces the Embodied First Exam (EFE), a framework that lets coding agents choose direct control, code-generated control, or policy training across 1,156 tasks in 35 suites and 47 simulated robots. It separates sensor-only Standard and Realtime settings from a Privileged setting with full simulator state and unlimited resets. On 391 core tasks with paired Privileged and Standard tests, the authors report GPT-6 Astra in Codex solved 77% in Privileged and 30% in Standard; adding resets to the Standard interface raised success to 53%, while adding both resets and exact object state raised it to 68%. These are preprint-reported simulation results, not independently reproduced physical-robot capability measurements.
